title: Signature Proof Lineage Archive
description: Signature edition: every proved theorem is archived with its full lineage — statement, proof script, prover version, dependencies, and what it was proved for. Proofs become permanent, re-checkable assets; future systems build on verified foundations instead of re-proving. This is a Signature original method.
method: Archive (statement, proof, prover version, deps) content-addressed; re-check on prover upgrades; index by what each theorem guarantees.
usage: Archive every production proof; re-check the archive when provers or dependencies change.

demo.code:
print('archived: add_comm, prover lean-4.8, deps: [Nat]')
print('prover upgraded -> re-check: still VALID')

title: Signature Dafny verification-aware language
description: Signature edition: Dafny bakes verification into the language: methods carry pre/postconditions, loops carry invariants, and the verifier (via Boogie and Z3) proves them at compile time. Code that doesn't verify doesn't compile — correctness checked as routinely as types.
method: Write specs as annotations; the verifier generates verification conditions; Z3 discharges them; failures point at the unproven annotation.
usage: Write specs alongside code; strengthen invariants until the verifier is satisfied; treat verifier errors as design feedback.

demo.code:
print('method Abs(x: int) returns (r: int)')
print('  ensures r >= 0;')
print('Dafny: verified — postcondition proved for all inputs')

title: Signature Verified compilation (CompCert)
description: Signature edition: CompCert is a C compiler proved correct in Coq: the generated assembly is proved to preserve the semantics of the source for every input. Integrating verified compilation means the toolchain itself can't introduce bugs — the strongest link in the verification chain.
method: Compiler passes proved as semantics-preserving simulations in Coq; the extracted compiler carries the proof; use for safety-critical builds.
usage: Use verified compilation for the critical components; the proof covers the compiler, not your source logic.

demo.code:
print('CompCert: 12 passes, each proved semantics-preserving')
print('build: critical controller compiled with CompCert -> no miscompilation possible')

title: Signature Proof replay in CI
description: Signature edition: Proofs rot like tests when code changes — proof replay re-runs the full mechanized proof suite on every commit, catching the moment a code change breaks a proof. The proof suite is a CI job like any other: green means the guarantees still hold.
method: Check in proof scripts with code; CI runs the proof checker; failures block merge; proof maintenance is part of the change.
usage: Keep proofs fast enough for CI (cache aggressively); assign proof repair with the code change.

demo.code:
print('CI: lean --make ... 142 theorems checked')
print('result: all proved in 38s -> MERGE')

title: Signature Model-based prover debugging
description: Signature edition: When the prover says 'can't prove it', its model (counterexample) shows a concrete scenario violating the property — often revealing the spec is wrong, not the code. Reading prover models turns failed proofs into debugging sessions instead of dead ends.
method: On failure, extract the solver's model; map it back to program variables; inspect: is the code wrong, or is the spec too strong?
usage: Always read the counterexample before weakening the spec; most failed proofs teach something.

demo.code:
print('failed: ensures result > 0')
print('model: x = 0 -> result = 0')
print('diagnosis: spec too strong (x=0 valid input) -> fix spec, re-prove: OK')

title: Signature Proof-carrying CI artifacts
description: Signature edition: Build artifacts ship with their proofs: the binary plus a machine-checkable certificate that it satisfies its spec. Downstream consumers verify the certificate in milliseconds without re-running the prover — trust the proof, not the build machine.
method: Prover emits (artifact, proof); the proof checker is small and fast; deployment gates on proof validity.
usage: Keep the checker tiny and audited; gate deployments on proof validity for critical components.

demo.code:
print('artifact: controller.bin + proof.cert')
print('deploy gate: checker verifies cert in 40ms -> VALID, deploy proceeds')

title: Signature Boogie intermediate verification language
description: Signature edition: Boogie is the shared intermediate layer: frontends (Dafny, VCC) compile programs and specs to Boogie, which generates verification conditions for Z3. One solid VC generator serves many languages — the LLVM of program verification.
method: Frontend emits Boogie (procedures + specs); Boogie computes weakest preconditions; Z3 proves them; errors map back to source.
usage: Build new verifiers on Boogie rather than from scratch; map errors back to source locations carefully.

demo.code:
print('Dafny -> Boogie -> VC -> Z3')
print('Boogie: 14 verification conditions, 14 proved')

title: Signature Coq/Lean proof assistant integration
description: Signature edition: Proof assistants (Coq, Lean) check human-guided proofs down to logical foundations. Integrations embed them in development: critical algorithms get mechanized proofs, and CI re-checks every proof on every commit — the proof is code, maintained like code.
method: State theorems; construct proofs with tactics; the kernel checks the proof term; CI runs the checker on every change.
usage: Prove the critical core, not everything; keep proofs robust to refactoring (avoid brittle tactic scripts).

demo.code:
print('Lean: theorem add_comm (a b : Nat) : a + b = b + a')
print('proof checked by kernel: OK — 0.4s in CI')

title: Signature Tactic-based proof automation
description: Signature edition: Tactics are proof-search programs inside assistants: 'simp', 'omega', 'ring' discharge whole classes of goals automatically. Good tactic libraries mean humans prove the interesting steps and automation handles the routine — the division of labor that makes mechanized proof affordable.
method: Apply domain tactics to goals; they perform search/simplification; remaining goals get human attention; custom tactics encode domain knowledge.
usage: Build a tactic library per domain; prefer robust tactics over brittle exact-step scripts.

demo.code:
print('goal: (a + b) * 2 = 2 * a + 2 * b')
print('tactic: ring -> CLOSED (no human steps needed)')
